schema_review.rationale: Revision v1_5_0_006 follows v1_5_0_005 on both registered source chains and all vector/Code profiles. It adds pc_source_runners (name, display name, registering principal type and identifier, nullable registration ID unique per principal, registration time, reported capabilities and digest, nullable last_seen_at) and pc_source_collect_targets (Scope and target identity, runner, capability, target key unique per Scope, runner and capability, parameters, enabled, configuration version, update audit, and runner-written status columns, including whether the last attempt left more to collect), and drops pc_source_write_plugins. The source_collection domain step refuses the upgrade while pc_source_write_plugins lists a plugin, so no loaded write plugin is lost silently; otherwise no existing record is rewritten. Earlier revision resources, frozen checksums and SQLite fingerprints are unchanged; the MySQL layout for the new tables is registered from the same SQLAlchemy DDL. Target checkpoints reuse pc_connector_checkpoints keyed by (scope_id, target_id) with a constant connector version; a commit for a collection target is validated against the target's runner, enabled state and configuration version in the transaction that writes the checkpoint and status. Portable bundles add source_runner (name, display name, registering principal and registration ID) and source_collect_target records; reported capabilities, last-seen time and target status restart empty. Revision v1_5_0_005 follows v1_5_0_004 on both registered source chains and all vector/Code profiles. It removes the storage of the previous Artifact plugin framework (family schemas, declarative search and vector index tables, and the plugin registration columns of pc_artifact_processing_binding_states) and adds the nullable pc_artifacts.metadata column, which records the plugin name and code digest of plugin-written revisions and stays NULL for built-in families. Its domain preflight refuses the upgrade while the previous framework still holds any registration, declaration or index row, and native maintenance refuses registered native vector spaces, so no data is dropped silently. Its readiness accepts directory-loaded 'plugin:' Processing bindings without durable registration and keeps the frozen built-in full-text checks; plugin families write no rows to pc_artifact_fts. Revision reads omit metadata so domain steps at earlier registered revisions still run. Portable Artifact revision records advance to schema version 3 with metadata, and version 2 records restore with metadata NULL. Earlier revision resources, fingerprints and checksums remain unchanged; local SQLite migration tests do not establish native seekDB/OceanBase or installed-release acceptance. Topic Memory processing failures attach bounded, content-free stage, reason and budget diagnostics to in-flight exceptions. Rejected reservations retain their existing durable charges; readback omits token-specific fields unless committed evidence establishes the limiting dimension, and repeated rejected calls cannot reinterpret prior evidence. Source structure and history-count guards do not imply context overflow. Missing FTS capability is configuration, and incomplete vector projections are business validation. No database schema, migration resource, registered table layout, frozen revision checksum, row encoding, persisted journal format or worker retry behavior is changed by these diagnostic annotations. The reusable Server migration framework registers actual PowerContext 1.3.0 through s1300 -> s1400 -> s1401 -> s1402 and actual 1.4.0 through the separate immutable r1400 -> s1400 -> s1401 -> s1402 source bridge. Original 1.3 resources and checksums remain byte-identical. Real 1.4.0 SQLite, embedded seekDB and OceanBase structures were captured from the official wheel in all twelve vector/Code configurations; provenance and exact source layouts are packaged with the bridge. The 1.4 bridge preserves current Candidate, Artifact and task data, adds the missing Topic budget/block structure, revokes old lease fences and joins the existing archive/portable-storage path. Empty retained tables align the final schema without inventing 1.3 Candidate history. Source histories retain their identity through subsequent upgrades and recovery; shared head names never authorize adopting unknown layouts. Vector profiles remain bound to historical model, profile ID, dimension, unit normalization and L2 distance, with no provider calls during maintenance. Complete schema, domain, projection, profile and retained-history checks precede startup and partial maintenance. Local SQLite and embedded seekDB startup reject an observable active maintenance lock through a read-only probe. SQLite runtime admission validates the default adjacent journal, rejecting unfinished full or partial maintenance, changed recorded revision checksums and missing required retained tables. Absent journals do not invent retention obligations; custom evidence directories require explicit operator verification and remote coordinator locks remain subject to deployment orchestration. Native read-only readiness uses a consistent snapshot and does not acquire Atomic Memory head locks; normal business transaction isolation is unchanged. Offline projection repairs retain the original locked state comparison and write-side CAS protection. Target locks, backup choices, original recovery evidence and explicit remote acknowledgments remain enforced. The installed-artifact catalog retains twelve 1.3.0 source/backend/vector/Code combinations. Embedded seekDB uses pylibseekdb 1.4.0.post2 or newer with the recovered-transaction lock fix. Main and publication require all twelve configurations, including embedded seekDB full-server-code and full-server-vector-code. No configuration is waived; incomplete, failed or skipped evidence rejects acceptance. The seekdb-code diagnostic selection cannot authorize publication. The registered 1.4.0 bridge remains implemented but is outside the CI upgrade acceptance matrix; passing this gate does not certify that path. The gate preserves source-specific Processing counters and isolates OceanBase source databases. Any failed, skipped or missing automatic case rejects publication. The policy remains upgrade-required until the exact target artifact passes the required automatic matrix and the reviewed support declaration is updated. Captured source structure, local tests and checkpoint replay are distinct from installed-release acceptance, native interruption/observer recovery and backup restoration. The Candidate generation prototype observes actual SQLite/seekDB/OceanBase migration checkpoints outside the production bundle; it does not replace frozen registrations or weaken recovery checks. Existing target schema and data formats, including batched persistence interfaces, remain governed by the shared registered path. The synchronized master adds blank-text validation at Source creation and managed worker logging. It changes neither registered table layout nor migration data encodings; existing stored Source values are not rewritten. The source bridges and frozen history remain unchanged. Compatibility commands identify Server-owned storage before opening a writable legacy profile and delegate source admission to the shared framework, including actual 1.4.0 and rejection of unknown layouts. Partial Processing and Atomic Memory projection maintenance verify the original recorded revision checksums; native admission also validates typed journal identity and its completed position against the database revision. Persisted vector profiles reject unsupported partial maintenance before plans, backups or operation evidence, including when the supplied configuration omits embeddings. These are admission-only changes; frozen migration resources, registered layouts, historical checksums and data transformations remain unchanged. PowerContext 1.4.1 assigns release-based presentation names v1_4_1_001 through v1_4_1_003 to the existing shared upgrade steps; the 1.3.0 and 1.4.0 source baselines remain independently registered. Existing revision IDs, bundle and revision checksums, accepted plan identities and journal schemas are unchanged. Unpublished Server schema changes accumulate in a shared 000 revision and its registered resources. Release preparation freezes this draft as v<major>_<minor>_<patch> after declaring the target version. Development databases are disposable; only supported released-version upgrades are promised. Revision descriptors parse this format while preserving historical release sequences, legacy aliases and opaque custom IDs. The sequence field is null for frozen release names and 000; the draft has no software_version. Historical sequence and PR-based names remain readable. Dependency order still follows down_revision. This naming support changes no registered schema, frozen resource, persisted revision, plan identity or checksum. Software releases without storage changes may reuse the same database revision. Naming does not grant acceptance or replace source registration. Full Server status, plan, apply and verify reject unfinished Processing configuration and Atomic Memory projection journals through the same typed admission check used by partial maintenance and SQLite startup. The owning domain runner can still resume its own journal. This only changes admission; frozen revisions, journal formats, database layouts and data transformations remain unchanged. Revision v1_4_1_004 registers the pc_access_owner_recovery outbox on the shared Server chain for both installed-release sources and all registered vector/Code profiles. It creates an empty table through explicit maintenance for existing managed databases and through the registered bootstrap for fresh databases. Earlier revision resources, fingerprints, checksums and existing domain row encodings remain unchanged. External relationship writers use version-1 Artifact and Candidate intents committed with domain data; replay retains the original deployment, principal, resource or target, and idempotency identity. Stable operation and audit event identities prevent lost acknowledgements from duplicating ownership or audit. Conflicting intents are rejected and unknown historical ownership is not inferred. Unregistered outbox layouts are not adopted merely from a table name. This registration does not establish installed-release or external-Provider upgrade acceptance. The policy remains upgrade-required with the full automatic matrix and publication restrictions described above. Database selection now defaults to powercontext for seekDB and for OceanBase URLs without a database, while explicit database names remain authoritative. An implicit seekDB selection is rejected before initialization when the legacy test database contains pc_ tables; operators can explicitly select database=test to retain those records, and no database is moved or deleted automatically. Bootstrap reuses an accessible selected database without CREATE privilege and creates only a confirmed missing database, with idempotent creation and explicit permission errors. Read-only maintenance on an initialized MySQL-compatible engine requires the selected database and never provisions it; an absent or empty seekDB instance remains a no-engine initial plan. MySQL initialization creates only missing requested tables and indexes, and sorts only those requested tables; existing registered tables are preserved. Code graph connections use the selected database, retain historical graph identities for test, and distinguish other database identities. Server identity initialization avoids redundant MySQL DDL on an existing table. Frozen migration resources, revision identifiers and checksums, registered table definitions, journal formats, and existing row encodings are unchanged. These runtime selection and admission changes do not establish an accepted upgrade path; the policy remains upgrade-required and the installed-release acceptance gate still applies. MySQL recovery rejects different registered table sets before normalization. Backend-default normalization copies only the column and index maps it changes and compares each table without cloning whole inventories. Admitted layouts, registered transitions, recovery checks, schema equality and caller-owned inventories remain preserved. SeekDB status and verify distinguish a missing configured database from an uninitialized engine and denied access. Read-only plan can represent a missing selected database as an uninitialized target without creating it; apply provisions that selected database only after the operator accepts its bound plan, then rechecks the target under the maintenance lock. Installed-release seekDB acceptance explicitly retains the historical test database and separately verifies that omitted selection is refused. Registered schema resources, revision checksums, row encodings and write-side provisioning remain unchanged. Server startup can apply an uninitialized plan to provision a missing selected seekDB database; plan, status and verify still never provision it. OceanBase 4.6 SHOW CREATE TABLE can reflect FTS_INDEX_TYPE=MATCH or PHRASE_MATCH on FULLTEXT indexes. Reflection accepts these known types without changing the logical inventory; unknown values remain rejected and indexed columns, parser identity and token-size properties remain significant. PHRASE_MATCH additionally supports phrase matching; the registered layouts require term matching and do not declare a phrase-only contract. Frozen migration resources, checksums, recovery evidence and persisted layouts remain unchanged. Native 4.6.3.1 DDL was captured from a real installed 1.3.0 database; replay of this fixture does not establish complete native upgrade acceptance. The CI database image and master full automatic upgrade matrix remain unchanged. Revision v1_4_1_005 adds nullable Atomic Memory description projection metadata after the registered owner-recovery revision, through explicit SQLite and MySQL schema transitions for both source chains and all vector/Code profiles. Earlier revision resources, fingerprints and checksums remain unchanged. The additive change neither rewrites authoritative Artifact history nor generates summaries or scans stored bodies. Existing managed databases require explicit migration; existing descriptions remain null until a new write or explicit projection repair copies authoritative metadata. Intermediate projection validation uses only columns available at that revision and still rejects inconsistent existing fields. Unmanaged SDK initialization retains its nullable-column compatibility path. The installed-release acceptance matrix and publication restrictions remain required; local regression checks do not establish native upgrade acceptance. Artifact plugin storage extends the shared Server chain from v1_4_1_006 to v1_5_0_001 with registration columns, family declarations, search state and projections, index coverage and changes, and vector-space/index registrations. SQLite also registers portable vectors and FTS auxiliary structures. Native registration columns are added in one ALTER with a matching recovery checkpoint; final column definitions and constraints are unchanged. Native vector tables are created online from registered spaces and are admitted to later maintenance inventories only after exact layout validation. Historical migration resources, retained objects, and existing data are preserved. This review does not expand the supported upgrade matrix or certify installed-release acceptance. Source write plugin registrations use the additive v1_4_1_006 revision after v1_4_1_005 on both source chains. It creates only pc_source_write_plugins; all earlier master revision scripts, schema resources and checksums remain unchanged. Revision v1_5_0_002 follows v1_5_0_001 and adds retained Source evidence bindings, exact Atomic Memory evidence snapshots and their schema marker on all registered backends. A new versioned domain step verifies retained evidence for lexical and vector profiles; earlier released domain resources and recorded revision checksums remain byte-identical. Existing Sources and Memory revisions without accepted declarations stay neutral, with no trust backfill. Current projection maintenance and rebuild explicitly require evidence validation. This additive registration does not establish installed-release acceptance; the upgrade-required gate and publication restrictions are unchanged. Revision v1_5_0_003 adds the disposable exact-revision pc_atomic_memory_evidence projection through the existing index adapters. Transactional body writes publish it from accepted evidence; scoped portable restore and maintenance rebuild derive it from retained history without current-registry trust backfill or model calls. Domain conformance compares historical and derived values, including neutral legacy declarations, on lexical and vector layouts. Earlier revision resources and fingerprints remain unchanged. Local SQLite recovery and real OceanBase 4.4.2.1 evidence conformance were exercised; these do not certify installed-release upgrades or change publication restrictions. Source evidence maintenance now accepts the deployment's own Source definition registry, reports one bounded neutralization reason through operational logs, batches exact-revision reads and caches retained-schema validation per manifest fingerprint. Indexed repair accepts that registry explicitly; the migration bundle still admits evidence against the builtin registry and says so. These changes alter neither registered table layouts nor retained encodings, and the runtime and Server evidence DDL remain byte-identical. The policy remains upgrade-required with the full automatic matrix and publication restrictions described above. Source definition manifests derive every field whose default is null from the validation schema, so an already accepted Definition keeps its fingerprint and re-registers after upgrade; populating such a field requires the nested model to serialize by alias. Registered layouts and retained encodings are unchanged. The runtime MySQL-family table fast path now runs the registered additive evidence migration before creating other tables, so an unmanaged OceanBase or seekDB database cannot retain evidence tables without their p0005 marker.. Code publication recovery adds an optional per-binding publication.json journal that records a generation identifier before its database commit and final directory rename. Caches created before this journal existed remain readable without synthesizing historical publication records; identifiers for already orphaned rows are not inferred. New seekDB generations retain the existing identifier, graph descriptor, manifest and row encodings, while reclamation validates the recorded identifier and scopes deletion to its binding. Live or reader-retained generation directories and the in-flight publication are protected from journal-window reclamation. SQLite graph rows remain owned by their generation directory. This additive local cache journal changes recovery behavior but does not change registered SQL table layouts, migration resources, revision identifiers, historical checksums or the Server migration journal. The policy remains upgrade-required, and the complete installed-release acceptance matrix remains mandatory; this compatibility review is not evidence of completed native upgrade acceptance. Managed Ops admission validates a private main-file and WAL snapshot through the exact target Server bundle, retaining the original database identity and maintenance evidence. Snapshot admission is read-only and cannot initialize, migrate or recover storage. It adds no schema revision, changes no persisted row or journal format, and does not expand supported upgrade declarations or the installed-release acceptance matrix. PreparedContext Receipt records the actual FTS mode on Experience search outcomes. This adds only an in-memory observation field; it does not change stored Experience rows, SQL selection, schema registrations, migration resources, or data encodings. Unmanaged historical Server databases are admitted by required structure and domain state, then normalized before adopting an existing checkpoint. Historical Memory conversion, Scope preservation, SQLite rollback and native DDL recovery use the shared maintenance flow. Independent extension objects and harmless DDL differences do not require clean-install fingerprints. Existing immutable revision resources and the installed-release acceptance matrix remain unchanged. Local historical tests do not certify arbitrary tenant defaults, every vector/Code configuration or future releases. SQLite compatibility validation includes effective primary-key collations and rejects conflicting identity semantics. Historical normalization and the frozen s1400 rebuild preserve generated extension definitions while copying only writable columns. Both virtual and stored generated values remain computed by SQLite; immutable revision resources and the native backend paths are unchanged. SQLite table rebuilds preserve declared collations on ordinary and generated extension columns, including their inherited index comparison semantics. Expression-local COLLATE clauses remain part of their expressions and do not change the column collation. This changes only SQLite compatibility normalization; frozen revisions and native backend execution remain unchanged. Historical Memory admission recognizes lineage ownership columns and default non-merge references while rejecting unmapped payloads. Native compatibility journals record temporary Processing counter ownership before DDL and clear it after cleanup, including completed-phase recovery. SQLite extension preservation also covers the registered r1400 bridge. Frozen migration resources and the installed-release acceptance matrix remain unchanged. Native historical Atomic conversion creates nullable description metadata with the registered UTF-8 binary collation, allowing the later frozen ADD transition to recognize its completed postcondition without duplicate DDL. SQLite historical normalization and registered source bridges preserve dependent views and their triggers during same-name table replacement. Legacy rename behavior is limited to the exact staging-to-final rename statements and the original connection setting is restored; genuine table renames still update dependent references. Frozen migration resources and native backend behavior remain unchanged. SQLite admission validates required extension defaults using SQLite deterministic-expression restrictions and a non-NULL evaluation on an isolated connection. Connection-state, random and clock-dependent expressions are rejected; direct CURRENT_DATE, CURRENT_TIME and CURRENT_TIMESTAMP defaults remain supported alongside usable constant expressions. Regression coverage verifies consecutive Source writes in distinct scopes within the same transaction. Read-only verification and startup admission share this rule; supported defaults remain usable through Source write and readback. Independent extension tables remain preserved through managed upgrades and initialization recovery; missing recovery evidence and missing vector configuration still block maintenance. Registered native column additions and modifications materialize the charset and collation declared by their immutable postcondition when the SQL would otherwise inherit a historical table default. This preserves GBK-origin upgrade recovery without changing frozen resources, existing table defaults, independent extension encodings or readiness requirements. SQLite Candidate extension columns and their values survive both stages of the registered Dream rebuild, including generated columns and dependent views. Frozen source introspection projects the already-validated managed columns without altering stored extension data. Independent indexes use SQLite-rewritten definitions after genuine table renames. Native CHECK removal resolves the actual constraint name from the registered expression and enforcement semantics, including recovery after committed DDL. Frozen resources, registered revision checksums and the installed-release acceptance matrix remain unchanged. SQLite admission rejects additional NOT NULL generated columns because computed values can reject valid Source writes. Nullable virtual and stored extensions remain preserved across historical upgrades and support Source write/readback. Frozen migrations and native backend behavior are unchanged. Ownership recovery preflight derives candidate-family filters from the exact migration identities, including Prompt Candidates that do not have standalone Artifact owners. Static Scope permission previews now use the same complete internal receipt keys as bootstrap for long Scope IDs. These authorization-only changes add no stored fields, row encoding, schema, or migration registration. Static Scope preset keys retain existing short identities and use SHA-256 for oversized relationship keys. Bootstrap and read-only preview recognize both bounded keys and historical receipts, including revoked bindings. No schema or migration registration changes. Managed observability reads existing Context Bootstrap receipt metadata in authorized Scope batches and aggregates it by integration and receipt state. This adds no schema revision, stored row changes, migration resources, or data encoding changes; receipt identities, historical evidence and the declared upgrade acceptance matrix remain unchanged. SQLite connection failures drain the aiosqlite 0.22.1 worker before propagating the error or cancellation, including failures before pool admission. This connection-lifecycle fix changes no registered schema, historical revision checksum, stored value, or upgrade source policy. Prepared-context reuse proofs revalidate cited code files by reading their current worktree digest through the existing no-follow capture reader and exclusion rules. This adds a read-only lookup; it changes no code index cache layout, manifest, graph rows, publication journal, SQL layout, migration resource or checksum. Revision v1_5_0_004 adds the optional pc_artifact_source_locators relation keyed by the existing Artifact Revision and Source-edge ordinal for both registered source releases and vector/Code profiles. Explicit maintenance creates the empty relation without rewriting historical lineage, payloads, Source identities, earlier revision resources or checksums. Missing locators remain omitted in legacy encodings; located citations survive persistence, HTTP/MCP and portable export/restore, and Source sequence mismatches are rejected without redirecting identity. Atomic Memory content and vector bindings are unchanged, so locator metadata does not require re-embedding. Local SQLite migration, restart, citation and portable round-trip tests pass; MySQL layout checks do not constitute native seekDB/OceanBase or installed-release acceptance. The upgrade-required policy, required automatic matrix and publication restrictions remain unchanged. Projection verification and repair read only the exact authoritative head content and state, avoiding target-only Source locator lineage tables at earlier registered migration checkpoints. Frozen resources and revision checksums remain unchanged. Source locator line-count and heading-path limits are centralized without changing their values, accepted payloads or stored encodings. Gateway authorization adds the Scope-level gateway.user role and gateway.invoke action to the existing binding vocabulary. It does not change stored binding structure or migration resources: existing records retain their role and do not implicitly gain gateway.invoke; new grants use the existing binding persistence and resource validation. Existing upgrade support remains upgrade-required and is not certified by this digest refresh. OceanBase Atomic Memory lexical retrieval uses native MATCH with minimum_should_match and SCORE when a controlled capability probe confirms support, and retains the existing MATCH AGAINST plus complete-word coverage path for unsupported backends. Capability decisions are held only in memory per connection pool. Search, complete related enumeration and recovery preserve Analyzer term deduplication, coverage thresholds, scope and content filters, vector completeness checks, same-statement authority heads and the existing oceanbase_match raw-score contract. This query-only change adds no tables, public interfaces, schema revisions, stored fields or row encodings; existing SPACE index definitions, projection formats, historical migration resources and revision checksums remain unchanged. No schema migration or projection rebuild is required for this query implementation. The upgrade-required policy, registered sources and complete installed-release acceptance matrix remain unchanged; this review does not certify installed-release upgrades. Queries above 256 distinct terms retain whole-word coverage unless the engine is identified as OceanBase 4.6 or newer, because earlier native engines can accept MATCH while ignoring that threshold. This compatibility guard changes query selection only. Native capability caching obtains the pool through run_sync, including pinned historical migration connections, without acquiring another connection or releasing maintenance locks. Queries containing SPACE stopwords retain Analyzer-based whole-word admission in all lexical operations. These corrections change neither stored projections nor registered schema resources. SQLite Topic Memory full-text helper version 2 assigns each Scope's helper rows to a hashed 2^32-rowid range above every rowid that version 1 assigned, so Topic replacement and search bound their FTS5 cursors to one Scope's range. Virtual table definitions, registered schema fingerprints, migration resources and authoritative active Topic rows are unchanged. Unmanaged initialization and the existing s1400 domain step rebuild version-1 helper rows from the active tables with exact identities and revisions; a managed database that still holds version-1 helper rows keeps the previous identity filters until the helper is rebuilt. bm25 statistics remain table-wide, so search hits, ordering and scores are unchanged. The standalone seekdb maintenance identity is derived from @@server_uuid and DATABASE() when ob_compatibility_mode is missing, NULL, or empty and VERSION() contains -OceanBase seekdb-. The db-migrate identity probe and the server-run tenant gate share one compatibility classifier; ORACLE and non-seekdb servers remain rejected. This is an admission-only change and does not alter registered table layouts, migration resources, persisted row encodings, or public interfaces. Source writes and text retrieval reuse parameterized SQL structures with fresh Scope, identity, revision, binding and increment values on every execution. Only the fixed built-in Content manifest construction and exact validated payload bytes reuse cached metadata; database registration and indexed-identity checks remain current, and callers receive deep copies. MySQL/OceanBase journal allocation retains SELECT FOR UPDATE; SQLite retains its write reservation. Concurrent Content captures coalesce already queued requests into bounded transactions, isolate individual failures after batch rollback, replay stable identities on cancellation and drain admitted callers during shutdown. No schema, migration, stored encoding, Source identity, journal ordering, processing counter semantics or upgrade support claims change. A Topic Memory window attempt whose publication loses the Topic head CAS to a concurrent replace or Dream records last_error_code head_conflict on its existing pc_topic_memory_work_budgets row, and the attempt ceiling and the next attempt's counter treat that one attempt as not spent. Provider request and token charges stay committed and are never refunded. No table layout, column, constraint, migration resource, revision checksum or row encoding changes; existing rows never carry head_conflict, so their counters and blocks keep their meaning. A binary without this change counts such an attempt as spent, which can only stop that frontier sooner. The Dashboard processing page reads the existing Source journal and Artifact lineage relation and marks only Sources with an exact Artifact citation. It introduces no new table or public JSON interface and does not reconstruct execution history, delivery or adoption. Source journal envelopes record an optional UTC saved_at timestamp for newly inserted records. This adds write metadata inside the existing powercontext-source-v1 payload, without changing registered tables, schema revisions, frozen migration resources or checksums. Historical envelopes and raw legacy payloads remain readable with unknown save time; replay does not invent a timestamp, and handoff receipt upgrades preserve the original timestamp. Source identity, material digests, journal positions and processing intent identities remain unchanged. This compatibility review does not establish installed-release upgrade acceptance; the upgrade-required policy and complete automatic matrix remain unchanged. Relocating access control from the Server package to the built-in runtime, removing the unused Source-cursor discovery query, and moving the code command out of the built-in Code package are code-organization changes. They change neither registered table layout nor migration data encodings: the generated table and index DDL for every persistence and access table is identical on the SQLite and MySQL dialects. Native MySQL schema recognition now requires the absence of core tables and columns removed by registered transitions before accepting a recovery prefix or completed revision. Independent extension tables and columns remain supported. This executes the existing v1_5_0_005 cleanup without changing frozen resources, revision checksums, stored encodings or the required installed-release acceptance matrix. Request-serving plugin hosts reconstruct authorization without requiring a background service identity; scheduled workers retain the explicit identity requirement. This changes only process-local authorization configuration, with no schema, migration, persisted encoding or upgrade support changes. OceanBase vector SQL parameters and literals serialize finite float32 arrays with orjson while retaining pyobvector dimension validation, reference readback and special-value handling. Vector column types and stored float32 values are unchanged. Source evidence bindings are inserted as a batch in the accepting Source transaction with the same exact identities and immutable declarations. Current Atomic Memory verification reads projection pages and vector presence while preserving authoritative content, state, tag, profile, evidence and vector-dimension checks under the existing snapshot contract. These changes introduce no schema revisions, registered migration resource changes, historical rewrites or new installed-release upgrade claims. The OceanBase and seekdb profiles gain a helper that builds engines for another database of the same tenant or instance with the deployment's connection settings; plugin hosts and Workers use it to open each plugin's own database. It reads and writes no core table and changes no schema, migration, persisted encoding or upgrade support. Migration refusal diagnostics now state that retained legacy plugin records have no supported in-place upgrade path; unloading or exporting does not clear them. This wording correction changes no schema, rejection criteria or data transformation. Native managed-schema compatibility compares required columns, indexes and normalized CHECK definitions without deep-copying unrelated extension tables. Validation remains read-only and preserves required-schema admission, caller-owned metadata and all registered schema, data and migration formats. The recurrence ledger exposes read-only queries over existing pc_recurrence_observation rows: observations_for_target returns one bucket, and event_counts_for_target aggregates its three event counts in SQL. Both filter by the indexed revision columns and by the signature hash plus its plaintext. They add no table, column, index, migration, stored encoding or write path, and existing ledger rows, upgrade acceptance cases and policy mode are unchanged. Complete Atomic Memory related enumeration admits a memory when the distinct candidate terms it contains meet the lexical threshold of the candidate's distinct terms, or number at least the minimum match count and cover the coverage fraction of the memory's own indexed words, so a long candidate reaches a short memory of the same fact; window siblings use the same rule. The per-row requirement is computed from the existing searchable text in SQL on SQLite, seekDB and OceanBase, and the native OceanBase path adds one MATCH block that applies whole-word coverage only to memories short enough to qualify below the candidate threshold. This threshold change leaves search, recovery probes, stored projections, registered schema resources and migrations unchanged. Plugin reloading can unregister, in the Server process, the Artifact access profile a plugin family registered when that plugin is removed or renames its family; built-in family profiles are never removed, and no table layout, migration resource, frozen checksum or persisted encoding changes. Atomic Memory evidence capture batches committed revisions in the existing transaction while preserving immutable first-writer histories, per-revision Source ownership and projection encoding. Historical Source reads join material and immutable bindings and batch retained manifests by exact definition version; a damaged ancillary manifest neutralizes only its own identity. Complete related vector recall validates all eligible projections and computes distances in one statement, rejecting invalid projections even outside the distance threshold. SQLite FTS query selection and impossible FTS recovery-probe short-circuiting change read execution only. No table, migration resource, stored encoding, journal order or installed-release upgrade support claim changes. Related hybrid ranks observe lexical results and complete vector validation in one SQL statement; page bodies and current authority remain separately admitted. Each backend prepares and decodes its rank query at one boundary; hybrid ranks retain RRF fusion when no lexical query can be formed. Single and batched active projection publication share current-tag loading under the caller transaction. Historical manifests use the same tolerant batch decoder for one or many identities. These read-execution changes preserve table layouts, stored formats, migrations and upgrade claims. Related hybrid ranks preserve the per-row lexical coverage rule of current related recall, including native full-text query blocks. No migration revision or persisted encoding changes. The 000 draft creates the private prepare diagnostic store with nullable Unicode query text included in the initial table definition. Earlier published resources and existing domain data remain unchanged. The public prepare response, public body-free Receipts, reuse and operational telemetry remain unchanged; diagnostics retain same-execution query and candidate/final text outside Source and Bootstrap storage, and capture adds no expiry or cleanup action. Schema transitions are additive and do not establish native installed-release acceptance. SQLite model-usage accounting classifies expiry during native-connection setup as an unapplied attempt, allowing the recorder to retry within its existing total write budget. No usage statement has executed at that boundary; indeterminate-commit handling and production deadlines remain unchanged. This changes no registered schema, migration resource, revision checksum, persisted row encoding, journal format, or declared upgrade support. Atomic Memory legacy recovery reads express lexical and semantic channel predicates in separate EXISTS query blocks within one scalar SQL statement. Scope and metadata eligibility, per-channel admission thresholds, invalid-vector precedence, bound-vector types and the consistent statement boundary are preserved. This changes read-query planning only: registered table layouts, projection formats, stored row encodings, migration resources, revision checksums and journal formats are unchanged. No migration or projection rebuild is required. The upgrade-required policy, registered source versions and full installed-release acceptance matrix remain unchanged; this review does not certify installed-release upgrades. OceanBase Experience, Atomic Memory and Topic Memory FULLTEXT initialization share the existing Topic Memory policy for transient native error 1205 during index creation. Each recovery attempt rechecks index existence before repeating only the derived-index DDL; subsequent projection refresh and capability validation still execute. Persistent conflicts and other errors remain failures, cancellation propagates, and the helper does not explicitly commit or roll back the caller or replay business writes. Native DDL transaction semantics are unchanged. Index definitions, registered table layouts, projection versions, stored row encodings, frozen migration resources, revision checksums and journal formats are unchanged. No migration or data conversion is required. Vector index initialization, the upgrade-required policy, registered source versions and all installed-release acceptance profiles are unchanged; this compatibility review does not certify installed-release upgrades. SQLite profile-owned cursors close a failed native statement on the existing database worker before propagating the original SQL error. This prevents cyclic exception collection from blocking the event loop while the same connection's worker waits for another writer.
